title: Fresh life-world sensing with boundary-ownership filter
objective: Resume white-portfolio ordinary-life sensing while explicitly rejecting formations whose apparent control plane is already naturally owned by platforms, communities, properties or public institutions.
truth_rules: A PLATFORM ALREADY STANDARDIZING TRUST IS STRONG COUNTEREVIDENCE
LOCATION/TIME CAN BE A ROUTING KEY

wide_scan.observed_pressure: pet owners repeatedly need care during travel/overtime while allowing a stranger into the home creates safety, privacy and animal-risk concerns

evidence.fact: A 2026 Wuhan report describes an upstart pet-home-care platform already covering 12 cities with 1,500+ signed pet sitters, continuous livestreaming, platform customer-service supervision and reported repeat purchase of 80–90%.

Other 2026 reporting describes strong holiday demand and explicitly identifies contracts, insurance, platform discipline and standardized rules as the industry's path from informal providers to professional service.

wide_scan.verdict: The trust boundary is real, but private platforms are already turning it into a standardized control plane. Do not rediscover pet care as a missing edge.

wide_scan.observed_pressure: dual-income parents face the 16:30 school-pickup gap while healthy retired residents have time, local presence and childcare experience

evidence.fact: The shared-grandmother model has appeared across multiple cities and is coordinated by communities as volunteer mutual aid.
A 2026 Zhejiang program set 17:30–19:00 precisely around the school/work timing gap; 35 child places across two communities filled in less than half a day.
Health Times reported in 2026 that community-coordinated shared-grandmother programs have become sustained mechanisms for pickup and after-school companionship.

wide_scan.verdict: Strong bilateral timing complementarity exists, but child safety and volunteer orientation make the community the natural coordinator. No private control plane is promoted.

wide_scan.observed_pressure: households buy low-frequency tools while nearby households simultaneously hold idle tools

evidence.fact: People's Daily proposed community shared toolboxes in August 2026 because buying rarely used tools is uneconomic and calling repair workers can cost more than the task.
Operating community tool corners in 2026 use donated/purchased inventory, simple self-registration and often no deposit or rental fee, with the community/property layer maintaining the stock.

wide_scan.verdict: The resource mismatch is real, but centralizing tools into a community-owned pool collapses the peer-to-peer routing problem and leaves weak private economics.

wide_scan.observed_pressure: community/public space is idle at certain hours while young adults want nearby low-cost learning, work and social space

evidence.fact: A 2026 community night-school case raised evening utilization from below 20% to 85% by reusing existing public rooms across time slots.
Yantai Laishan reports a tiered public-space operating model and 330+ projects using qualified third-party operators, including low-cost evening programs.
Tianfu New Area is actively seeking uses/operators for more than 500,000 square meters of idle community carriers.

wide_scan.verdict: The time-shifted space mismatch is large, but the asset owner/community already controls access and is directly recruiting operators. A generic space-routing platform is not retained.

actors: outgoing renter facing move/disposal cost and residual-value loss
incoming renter facing setup/procurement cost and time
landlord/property actor seeking low-vacancy, low-friction turnover
wide_scan.observed_exchange: furniture/appliances and other room-specific items are transferred or gifted together with a rental succession because their value is materially higher in the same dwelling than after disassembly, transport or disposal

evidence.fact: A current 2026 Shenzhen transfer listing explicitly offers furniture with the room ('转租可送家具'), showing that room succession and residual household assets are already bundled in real tenant behavior.

A 2026 Shenzhen renter profile reports a tenant spending more than RMB 10,000 furnishing an initially sparse rental, then being relocated for work after ten months; because taking the furniture was impractical, she transferred it to the next tenant at roughly 70% of cost and personally helped the landlord find that successor.

2026 university graduation flea markets repeatedly describe the need to lighten luggage and solve the disposal/movement of items graduates cannot take away, showing a recurrent transition-event pump for residual assets even though campus markets are not the same formation.

structural_hypothesis.proposition: The dwelling/address plus lease-turnover event may be a stronger routing key than item category. The most efficient buyer for some bulky or fit-specific assets may be the next occupant of the exact same dwelling.

candidate_latent_outcomes.outgoing_renter: recover residual value while avoiding dismantling, transport, disposal and time cost
candidate_latent_outcomes.incoming_renter: reduce setup cost/time and gain items already fitted to the dwelling
candidate_latent_outcomes.landlord_or_operator: reduce vacancy/turnover friction and preserve a more move-in-ready unit

counterevidence.fact: The same current rental listing already carries furniture-transfer information, indicating that existing rental marketplaces can bundle the flow without a new platform.

A well-documented Shenzhen transfer case from 2023 showed furniture discounted from 80% to effectively free yet still failing to create a successor tenant when the underlying housing demand did not match.
Large rental platforms already bundle transition services such as moving and cleaning into graduate-rental offerings, showing incumbents can expand around the move event.

not_yet_evidenced: frequency/density of same-dwelling asset succession across mainstream mainland rentals
residual value net of condition, depreciation and landlord constraints
whether outgoing and incoming tenants overlap in time often enough
whether landlord/property/rental platform is already the natural control-plane owner
whether a missing edge exists beyond simply adding furniture notes to a transfer listing
whether settlement, inventory, consent or timing failure is repeated and costly
who would pay for orchestration and how much
whether economics survive outside high-churn rental districts
wide_scan.next_test: Run causal descent on the lease-turnover event. Determine whether the governing friction is housing succession itself, disposal/transport economics, inventory/condition trust, landlord consent, timing overlap, or fragmented cross-platform discovery. Kill the formation if current rental/property actors already solve the useful boundary at low marginal cost.

cross_scan_verdict.meta_learning: Community/public-resource formations repeatedly collapse into natural institutional control planes. The search should preferentially inspect transition boundaries where neither side naturally owns the handoff.

requirements: separate housing-transfer demand from residual-asset demand
test whether exact-address succession materially changes asset value
identify current control-plane owner at the turnover event
look for repeated failed handoffs, not attractive anecdotes
quantify transaction value and orchestration margin before promotion
do not design a marketplace, escrow, inventory tool or moving service yet
